page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-16 is an arm64 virtual machine instance powered by the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped directly to 16 physical cores, operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz with a single thread per core. The system is equipped with 64 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong memory subsystem performance. It achieves a top-tier PassMark memory score and strong uncached large-block read and write bandwidths of 259.29 GB/sec and 113.31 GB/sec, respectively. Multi-core compute capabilities are also strong, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 16780.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 190.59 GB/sec. Single-core performance and web serving throughput remain in the average tier.

The dedicated ARM architecture offers high resource density and energy efficiency. This hardware profile is effective for multi-threaded applications, database operations, text processing, and general-purpose web serving where consistent CPU allocation and high memory bandwidth are required.
